mainTopic: Holy objects and waste near קריאת שמע and תפלה, טבילה for a בעל קרי with a severe טומאה, and the time limits and make-up rules for תפלה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ruling about holy objects in a couple's room. רבי יהושע בן לוי requires a ten-טפחים partition for a ספר תורה, and the story with מר זוטרא shows this is only for someone with no other room. The גמרא then explains the משנה's four-אמות distance from waste: four אמות is enough behind you, but waste in front must be out of sight, for both קריאת שמע and תפלה. After several challenges, רב חסדא's permission to pray facing a bathroom is explained as being about a brand-new, unused one, and רבא adds that Persian bathrooms count as sealed. A new משנה asks whether someone with a severe טומאה who also has קרי must immerse, and the גמרא shows that רבי יהודה exempts him in either order. The פרק מי שמתו ends, and the new פרק opens with the time limits for each תפלה. The גמרא explains that שחרית may be said all day, but the reward for praying on time ends at חצות. It concludes that a missed תפלה can be made up at the next one if it was missed by mistake, but not if it was skipped on purpose.

steps.title: A cloak spread over a chest counts as a vessel within a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion: according to רבא, a cloak spread over the items on a chest is treated like a vessel inside another vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: (רבא said: a cloak) on a chest is like a vessel within a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the previous discussion. רבא's ruling: a cloak spread over holy items on a chest counts as covering them twice, like a vessel inside a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, the גמרא was asking how a holy object must be covered in a couple's room. The new point is that a cloak over a chest gives two layers; since a cloak is not the items' own designated container, it counts as a real second covering. That makes the object count as 'double-covered.'

keyTerms.meaning: A chest or box
A vessel within a vessel (double covering)
Is like, is considered as

phrases.english: (A cloak) on a chest is like a vessel within a vessel. (The word 'cloak,' גְּלִימָא, is at the end of the previous amud.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Placing a holy object on a chest gives it the status of a vessel within a vessel.

steps.title: A ספר תורה in the room needs a ten-handbreadth partition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a ספר תורה in a couple's room needs a partition ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: For a ספר תורה, one must make a partition of ten handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a new rule. If there is a ספר תורה in the room, a partition ten טפחים high must be built around it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering it the way one covers smaller holy items is not enough for a ספר תורה because it is holier. A partition ten טפחים high counts in הלכה as a separate area, so the ספר תורה is treated as if it were in another space.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scroll
A partition or divider
Ten (טְפָחִים, handbreadths)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A Torah scroll:
One must make a partition of ten for it.
phrases.notes: Ten means ten טפחים, roughly a meter. At that height the partition counts as a real divider.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ מְחִיצָּה עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from smaller holy items to a ספר תורה, which needs a stronger solution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ספר תורה in a couple's room needs a partition ten טפחים high.

steps.title: מר זוטרא sees a partition in מר בר רב אשי's room
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא visits רב אשי's house and sees that מר בר רב אשי built a ten-טפחים partition for a ספר תורה in his room.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא came to the house of רב אשי. He saw the room of מר בר רב אשי, where a ספר תורה was kept, and a ten-handbreadth partition had been made for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that puts רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule into practice. This step sets the scene for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר רב אשי was following רבי יהושע בן לוי exactly. The story is building toward a question about when this rule is really meant to apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come, visited
He saw it
Place, room

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Mar Zutra happened to come to the house of Rav Ashi,

phrases.aramaic: חַזְיֵיהּ לְדוּכְתֵּיהּ דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: he saw the room of Mar bar Rav Ashi
in which a Torah scroll was placed,
and he had made a partition of ten for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule being followed in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: the partition was built in practice.

steps.title: Why build a partition if you have another room?
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא asks whose view this follows, and points out that רבי יהושע בן לוי only allowed a partition for someone with no other room.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: According to whom? According to רבי יהושע בן לוי? Say that רבי יהושע בן לוי meant this only for someone who has no other room. But you, sir, do have another room!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges what he saw. He argues that the partition is only a fallback for someone without a second room, and מר בר רב אשי does have one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא narrows רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. The partition is a last resort and not the first choice. The better choice is to move the ספר תורה to another room.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?
Say (that is, perhaps this applies only...)
Another room

phrases.english: He said to him: In accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi?

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said it
for one who does not have another room,

phrases.aramaic: מָר הָא אִית לֵיהּ בֵּיתָא אַחֲרִינָא?
phrases.english: but you, Master, do have another room!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ כְּמַאן כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the action described in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's use of a partition when he had another room
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי's partition is only for someone with no alternative. With a second room available, the ספר תורה should be moved there.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that the partition is a fallback, and the better practice is to keep a ספר תורה in a separate room.

steps.title: I did not think of that
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי admits he had not thought of moving it, which accepts מר זוטרא's point.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It did not occur to me.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי answers that the idea had not crossed his mind. He agrees with מר זוטרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not defend the partition, so מר זוטרא's limit stands. The rule is now settled: use a partition only when there is no other room.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not on my mind

steps.whatToRemember: A partition for a ספר תורה is a fallback. If you have another room, the ספר תורה belongs there.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was not on my mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to מר זוטרא's challenge by accepting it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why use a partition when another room is available?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It simply had not occurred to him. He concedes the point.

steps.title: The משנה: keep four אמות away from waste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: one must stay four אמות away from urine and feces.
steps.simpleTranslation: How far must one distance himself from them and from feces? Four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It asks how far one must be from urine and feces to say קריאת שמע, and the answer is four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the base rule that the coming steps will explain and limit. Everything that follows builds on this four-אמות distance.

keyTerms.meaning: He must distance himself
Feces, waste
Four cubits (about 2 meters)

phrases.english: How far must one distance himself from them and from feces?
phrases.notes: 'From them' means from urine, which the משנה mentioned just before.

phrases.english: Four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה יַרְחִיק מֵהֶן וּמִן הַצּוֹאָה אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must be four אמות away from urine and feces.

steps.title: Four אמות only when the waste is behind you
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the משנה: four אמות is enough only behind you. In front, the waste must be out of sight, and the same is true for תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב סחורה, in the name of רב הונא: They taught this only for waste behind him. But if it is in front of him, he must move until it is out of sight. The same applies to prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains that the משנה's four אמות is only for waste behind a person. If it is in front, he must be far enough that he cannot see it at all, and this also applies to תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is now split in two. Behind you, four אמות is enough. In front of you, the distance is 'as far as the eye can see,' and this stricter rule also covers שמונה עשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this for...
Behind him
His full range of sight
Prayer (שמונה עשרה)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Seḥora said that Rav Huna said:
They taught this only for behind him,
but in front of him, he distances himself the full range of his eyes,
and the same is true for prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לַאֲחוֹרָיו אֲבָל לְפָנָיו מַרְחִיק מְלֹא עֵינָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's four-אמות rule to waste behind a person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waste in front of a person must be completely out of sight, for both קריאת שמע and תפלה.

steps.title: But רב חסדא allows praying facing a bathroom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with רב חסדא's ruling that one may stand facing a bathroom and pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: A person may stand facing a bathroom and pray!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's rule. רב חסדא allows praying while facing a bathroom, even though a bathroom is in front of you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says waste in front of you must be completely out of sight. A bathroom is a place of waste, so רב חסדא seems to say the opposite. The two rulings look like they contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (opens a challenge)
But didn't he say...?
Bathroom, outhouse

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי?! וְהָא אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא
phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Rafram bar Pappa say
that Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹמֵד אָדָם כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא וּמִתְפַּלֵּל!
phrases.english: A person may stand opposite a bathroom and pray!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's 'out of sight' rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that waste in front must be fully out of sight during תפלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא allows praying directly facing a bathroom. That conflicts with requiring waste in front to be out of sight.

steps.title: A bathroom with no waste in it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא was talking about a bathroom with no waste in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A bathroom that has no feces in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רב חסדא means a bathroom that is empty of waste, so רב הונא's rule does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's strictness is about actual waste. If the bathroom has none, there is nothing to stay away from, and the two rulings no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
That does not have in it

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With a bathroom that has no feces in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ צוֹאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing רב חסדא's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא allows praying facing any bathroom, which would contradict רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא only means a bathroom with no waste in it.

steps.title: An empty bathroom is still a bathroom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: רב יוסף בר חנינא says a bathroom keeps its status even with no waste, just as a bathhouse does even with no one inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב יוסף בר חנינא said: The bathroom the חכמים spoke of means even one with no feces, and the bathhouse they spoke of means even one with no person in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. רב יוסף בר חנינא teaches that a bathroom counts as a bathroom even when empty of waste, so the answer in step 9 fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 9 depended on an empty bathroom being treated differently. רב יוסף בר חנינא says that whenever the חכמים mention a bathroom, even an empty one is included. So the contradiction between רב הונא and רב חסדא comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: That they (the Sages) spoke of
Even though
Bathhouse

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Rav Yosef bar Ḥanina say:
The bathroom that they spoke of

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ צוֹאָה
phrases.english: means even if there is no feces in it,
and the bathhouse that they spoke of,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אָדָם!
phrases.english: means even if there is no person in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב חסדא meant a bathroom with no waste
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bathroom keeps its status even when it is empty of waste, so the emptiness cannot explain why praying facing it would be allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rules of the חכמים about a bathroom apply only when waste is actually there. Even an empty bathroom counts.

steps.title: A brand-new bathroom that was never used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: רב חסדא was talking about a new bathroom that has never been used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with here? A new one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first answer and gives a better one. רב חסדא meant a newly built bathroom that has not yet been used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A used bathroom keeps its status even after it is emptied. A bathroom that was never used has not taken on that status yet. So one may pray facing it, and רב הונא's rule stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer)
New ones (a new, unused bathroom)

steps.whatToRemember: Behind you, four אמות from waste is enough. In front of you, it must be out of sight. רב חסדא's permission to pray facing a bathroom is about a brand-new one that has never been used.

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
With new ones.
phrases.notes: He means a bathroom that was built but has not been used yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 9 with a new way to read רב חסדא's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New limiting case (אוקימתא) replacing the earlier one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא meant a bathroom that happens to be empty of waste.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא meant a newly built bathroom that has never been used.

steps.title: Does setting aside a room as a bathroom already count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'new bathroom' answer, because רבינא was unsure whether designating a room as a bathroom already gives it bathroom status.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבינא asked about exactly this: if someone set aside a room to be a bathroom, what is the law? Does setting it aside count, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer (a new, unused bathroom). רבינא was unsure about a room that was only set aside as a bathroom, so how could רב חסדא simply allow praying facing it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said רב חסדא permitted only a new, never-used bathroom. But a new bathroom has already been set aside for that use, and רבינא left open whether that alone makes it a real bathroom. If that is an open question, רב חסדא's simple permission looks hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: He designated it, meaning he set it aside for a certain use
Designation, setting something aside for a purpose
He asked about it as an open question

phrases.english: But Ravina asked about this as an open question:
If one designated it as a bathroom, what is the law?
Does designation count, or does designation not count?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 11 that רב חסדא spoke of a new bathroom
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב חסדא permitted only a new, unused bathroom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבינא was unsure whether designation alone gives bathroom status, so a new bathroom should not be clearly permitted.

steps.title: רבינא's doubt was only about praying inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבינא was only unsure about praying inside a designated bathroom. Praying facing it was never in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבינא asked his question, it was about standing and praying inside it. But about praying facing it, he had no question.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing רבינא's question. His doubt was only about praying inside the new bathroom, not about praying facing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases: praying inside a designated bathroom and praying facing it. רבינא was only unsure about the stricter case, being inside. Facing a new bathroom is clearly allowed, so רב חסדא's ruling about a new bathroom stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To stand
To pray
Inside it
Facing it, opposite it

steps.whatToRemember: A new, unused bathroom: facing it in תפלה is allowed. Praying inside it is the open question of רבינא.

phrases.english: When Ravina raised his question,
it was about standing to pray inside it,
but about facing it, no.
phrases.notes: He means: about praying facing it, רבינא had no question at all. It is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבינא's question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא was unsure whether a designated bathroom has any bathroom status at all, even for facing it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבינא's doubt was only about praying inside; facing a new bathroom is clearly permitted, so the answer about רב חסדא holds.

steps.title: Persian bathrooms count as covered
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that Persian bathrooms count as covered, even when there is waste in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These Persian bathrooms, even though they have waste in them, are treated as if they were sealed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling about one type of bathroom. Persian bathrooms are treated like covered ones, even if they have waste in them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a bathroom with waste causes a problem for תפלה nearby. רבא says Persian bathrooms are an exception and count as 'sealed', because they were built so the waste rolled away out of sight.

keyTerms.meaning: Persians
Human waste
They are considered as sealed or covered

steps.whatToRemember: Persian bathrooms are treated as covered, even with waste in them.

phrases.english: Rava said:
These bathrooms of the Persians,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית בְּהוּ צוֹאָה —
phrases.english: even though there is waste in them,
are considered as sealed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final ruling about one type of bathroom after the discussion of רב חסדא ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Persian bathrooms are treated as sealed, even when they contain waste.

steps.title: Severe impurity combined with the impurity of קרי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a זב who had a seminal emission, a נדה who discharged semen, and a woman who had relations and then saw נדה blood all need טבילה. רבי יהודה exempts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A זב who saw קרי, a נדה who discharged semen, and a woman who had relations and then saw נדה blood all need to immerse. רבי יהודה exempts them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It covers people who already have a severe טומאה and then also pick up the טומאה of קרי, and asks whether they still need טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people cannot become fully טהור by immersing now, because their bigger טומאה remains. The first opinion says they still must immerse because of the קרי. רבי יהודה exempts them, since immersion cannot fix their main טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with an unusual bodily discharge, which makes him impure for at least seven days
A seminal emission
A woman impure from menstruation
She discharged semen
A woman who had marital relations
Immersion in a מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: Immersing here does not make these people fully טהור. The question is only whether they must immerse because of the קרי while their bigger טומאה is still there.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A zav who experienced a seminal emission,
and a menstruating woman who discharged semen,
and a woman who had relations and then saw menstrual blood,
all require immersion.
And Rabbi Yehuda exempts them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those already in a severe טומאה who also have the טומאה of קרי need טבילה; רבי יהודה exempts them.

steps.title: What about a בעל קרי who later became a זב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה would rule when the order is reversed: first קרי, then זיבה. It lays out both sides of the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: a בעל קרי who then saw זיבה, what is the law according to רבי יהודה? Maybe רבי יהודה exempted the זב who saw קרי only because he was never fit for immersion from the start. But a בעל קרי who then saw זיבה was fit for immersion at first, so maybe he must immerse. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about רבי יהודה's view in the משנה. It sets out two possible ways to understand his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the זב already had the bigger טומאה before the קרי came, so immersion never worked for him. In the new case, the person first had only קרי, so at that moment he was fit to immerse, and only later became a זב. The question is whether that early moment keeps his obligation to immerse, or whether רבי יהודה exempts him either way.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
A man who had a seminal emission
The discharge that makes a man a זב
From the start, at first
Fit for immersion, someone immersion can help
Or perhaps there is no difference

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the possible reason behind רבי יהודה's exemption: maybe what matters is whether the person was fit for immersion when the קרי obligation first started.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was raised before them:
One who had a seminal emission and then saw a zav discharge,
according to Rabbi Yehuda, what is the law?
When Rabbi Yehuda exempted there,
in the case of a zav who saw a seminal emission,
it is because from the start he was not fit for immersion.
But one who had a seminal emission and then saw a zav discharge,
who at first was fit for immersion, would he require him to immerse?
Or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a new question about רבי יהודה's view in the משנה of step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה exempt a בעל קרי from immersion when he became a זב only after the קרי, since he was fit for immersion at first?

steps.title: Proof from the woman who had relations and then saw נדה blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings proof from the משנה's last case. A woman who had relations and then saw נדה blood is the same pattern as a בעל קרי who later saw זיבה, and רבי יהודה exempts her. So he exempts in the reverse order too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'A woman who had relations and then saw נדה blood needs טבילה, and רבי יהודה exempts.' Isn't that just like a בעל קרי who then saw זיבה? And רבי יהודה exempts. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16 by pointing to the third case of the משנה we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 we asked whether רבי יהודה still exempts when the קרי came first and the זיבה came after. The woman's case has that same order: first relations (like קרי), then נדה blood (the heavier טומאה). Since רבי יהודה exempts her, he must exempt the reverse-order case too.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who had marital relations
"Is like / is comparable to": the wording used to compare two cases
"Learn from it": the proof is accepted

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new case. It is the same third case from the משנה in step 15, now used as evidence because its order matches our question.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A woman who had relations and then saw menstrual blood requires immersion,
and Rabbi Yehuda exempts her.
Now isn't a woman who had relations and then saw menstrual blood
just like a man who had a seminal emission and then saw a zav discharge?
And Rabbi Yehuda exempts.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע הַמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת וְרָאֲתָה נִדָּה צְרִיכָה טְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 16 using the משנה quoted in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה exempts from טבילה even when the קרי came before the זיבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The third case of the משנה: a woman who had relations and then saw נדה blood, where רבי יהודה exempts.

steps.title: רבי חייא teaches the case explicitly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי חייא states our exact case: a בעל קרי who then saw זיבה needs טבילה, and רבי יהודה exempts. This confirms the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught it outright: a בעל קרי who then saw זיבה needs טבילה, and רבי יהודה exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the proof with a teaching that says the answer in plain words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 reached the answer by comparing two cases. Here רבי חייא's ברייתא names the case of קרי followed by זיבה directly and gives רבי יהודה's exemption, so no comparison is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, outright

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, once a person has a heavier טומאה like זיבה or נדה, a lighter קרי does not add a separate need for טבילה. The order of the two does not change this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught this explicitly:
One who had a seminal emission and then saw a zav discharge
requires immersion,
and Rabbi Yehuda exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms step 17's proof with a direct source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה exempts a בעל קרי who later saw זיבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רבי חייא.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing מי שמתו
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the third פרק of ברכות, מי שמתו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, מי שמתו.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק of מי שמתו ends here with the traditional closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is said at the end of each פרק as a promise to come back and learn it again. The next line opens a new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": said when finishing a perek
Name of the third perek of ברכות, taken from its first words

phrases.english: We will return to you, "One whose dead"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek after the last sugya is settled.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The perek מי שמתו is complete.

steps.title: The time limits for each daily prayer
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a משנה that sets the latest time for each תפלה. For שחרית, מנחה and מוסף, רבי יהודה gives an earlier deadline than the חכמים. ערבית has no fixed time.
steps.simpleTranslation: שחרית may be said until midday. רבי יהודה says until four hours into the day. מנחה may be said until evening. רבי יהודה says until פלג המנחה. ערבית has no fixed time. מוסף may be said all day. רבי יהודה says until seven hours.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה listing how late you may say each of the daily תפלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three disagreements. For each, the unnamed first view (the חכמים) gives a later deadline and רבי יהודה gives an earlier one. ערבית is different from the others because it is not tied to a set time.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, "our משנה"
Midday
The midpoint of the afternoon period
Has no fixed time
The extra תפלה said on שבת, יום טוב and ראש חודש

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the basis for the deadlines of the daily תפלות. The גמרא will go on to explain each opinion.
steps.confusionAlert: Hours here are counted from the start of the day, so "four hours" means four hours into the day, not 4:00 on the clock.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The morning prayer may be said until midday.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: until four hours into the day.
The afternoon prayer may be said until evening.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: until the midpoint of the afternoon.
The evening prayer has no fixed time.
And the additional prayer may be said all day.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: until seven hours into the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new perek after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחרית: until midday (רבי יהודה: four hours). מנחה: until evening (רבי יהודה: פלג המנחה). ערבית: no fixed time. מוסף: all day (רבי יהודה: seven hours).

steps.title: A ברייתא says the morning מצוה is right at sunrise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets a ברייתא against the משנה. The ברייתא says the מצוה is to say קריאת שמע at sunrise so that גאולה leads straight into תפלה, which means תפלה comes right at the start of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a contradiction: a ברייתא teaches that the מצוה of the morning שמע is right at sunrise, so that a person joins the ברכה of redemption to the תפלה and ends up praying as the day begins. That sounds much earlier and tighter than the משנה's deadline.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with the משנה's time for שחרית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a wide window for שחרית, until חצות or four hours. The ברייתא describes the מצוה as happening right at sunrise, with שמע and תפלה joined together. So which is it: a wide window, or right at sunrise?

keyTerms.meaning: And they set it against: the גמרא brings a source that seems to contradict the משנה
Sunrise, when the sun first shows over the horizon
Joining the ברכה of redemption (גאל ישראל) directly to the עמידה
Redemption, here meaning the ברכה after שמע that ends גאל ישראל

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they raised a contradiction:
Its מצוה is with sunrise,
so that he will join redemption to prayer,
phrases.notes: "Redemption" is the ברכה after שמע that ends גאל ישראל, said right before the עמידה.

phrases.english: and he will find himself praying in the daytime!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's deadline for שחרית from Step 20 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wide time window for שחרית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the מצוה is right at sunrise with שמע joined to תפלה, how can the משנה allow שחרית hours later?

steps.title: The sunrise rule is for the extra-careful ותיקין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא describes the practice of the ותיקין, the especially careful people. רבי יוחנן confirms that the ותיקין would finish שמע exactly at sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא was taught about the ותיקין. As רבי יוחנן said: the ותיקין would finish the שמע right at sunrise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: the ברייתא describes the best, most careful way, not the basic deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources talk about different levels. The ברייתא describes the ideal practice of the ותיקין, while the משנה gives the outer limit for everyone. רבי יוחנן's statement proves that this sunrise practice belonged to the ותיקין.

keyTerms.meaning: Especially careful and devoted people who do מצוות in the best way
Would finish (here, finishing שמע right at sunrise)

steps.confusionAlert: The ותיקין are not setting a deadline for everyone. Praying at sunrise is the best way, but the משנה's later time is still valid.

phrases.english: That one was taught for the vatikin.
As Rabbi Yochanan said:
The vatikin would finish it
with sunrise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special group (the ideal practice of ותיקין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא sets the required time for everyone, which would clash with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא describes the ideal practice of ותיקין. The משנה gives the basic deadline for everyone.

steps.title: Can שחרית really only be said until חצות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether everyone agrees that שחרית ends at חצות. רבי יוחנן says that someone who missed שחרית prays two at מנחה, which suggests שחרית can still be made up in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does everyone hold that שחרית is only until חצות and no later? But רב מרי, son of רב הונא, son of רבי ירמיה בר אבא, said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone made a mistake and did not pray ערבית, he prays two at שחרית. If he missed שחרית, he prays two at מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that חצות is the absolute end of שחרית, using רבי יוחנן's rule about making up a missed תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the חכמים, the more lenient side, end שחרית at חצות. But רבי יוחנן lets a person make up a missed שחרית at מנחה time, in the afternoon. If a שחרית תפלה can still count then, חצות does not seem to be a true cutoff.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone, meaning all opinions
Midday, the middle of the day
And no more, meaning not later
Made a mistake, here forgetting or missing a תפלה
Prays two עמידות, one to make up the missed תפלה

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עַד חֲצוֹת וְתוּ לָא,
phrases.english: And does everyone hold until midday and no more?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Mari, son of Rav Huna,
son of Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba,
say that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who erred and did not pray the evening prayer
prays two in the morning prayer,
if the morning prayer, he prays two in the afternoon prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עַד חֲצוֹת וְתוּ לָא, וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the משנה's deadline (Step 20), this time about the latest time rather than the earliest.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that שחרית can only be said until חצות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן lets a missed שחרית be made up at מנחה, so a שחרית תפלה still counts after חצות.

steps.title: Praying all day, but the reward for 'on time' ends at חצות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one may pray שחרית the whole day. Until חצות he gets the reward of praying in its proper time. After that he still gets the reward for praying, but not for praying on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may keep praying through the whole day. Until חצות, he is given the reward of a תפלה said in its proper time. From then on, he is given the reward of a תפלה, but not the reward of a תפלה said in its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by splitting the reward into two levels: 'prayer' and 'prayer on time.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deadline of חצות does not make a later תפלה worthless. It only marks the end of the 'on time' reward. So the משנה's deadline and רבי יוחנן's make-up rule do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He keeps on praying, meaning he may still pray
The reward for a תפלה said in its proper time
From here on, meaning after this point

steps.whatToRemember: The ideal is sunrise (ותיקין). The proper deadline is חצות (or four hours for רבי יהודה). After that one may still pray שחרית and get reward for praying, but not the reward of praying on time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea in הלכות תפלה: a time limit can mark 'on time' versus 'late' without cancelling the תפלה completely.

phrases.english: He may keep on praying the whole day,
until midday, they give him
the reward of prayer in its time;

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ, שְׂכַר תְּפִלָּה — יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: from here on, the reward of prayer they give him,

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכַר תְּפִלָּה בִּזְמַנָּהּ — לָא יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: the reward of prayer in its time they do not give him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יוחנן's make-up rule in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the law into levels (any reward for praying versus the reward for praying on time)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חצות is a hard cutoff, so after it שחרית cannot be said at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: שחרית may be said all day. חצות only ends the extra reward of praying in its proper time.

steps.title: Can a missed מנחה be made up at ערבית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether someone who missed מנחה by mistake may pray two at ערבית. It explains both sides of the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: someone mistakenly did not pray מנחה. May he pray two at ערבית? Even if a missed ערבית is made up at שחרית, that may be because night and the next morning are one day. Here, though, מנחה and ערבית fall on different days, and since תפלה is in place of a קרבן, once the day is over its קרבן is gone. Or maybe, since תפלה is asking for mercy, a person may keep praying whenever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: if you missed מנחה by mistake, can you make it up by praying two at ערבית? It then lays out the reason to say no and the reason to say yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making up ערבית at שחרית is easy to accept, because the night and the following morning count as one day. Making up מנחה at ערבית crosses into a new day. If תפלה works like a קרבן, a new day means it's too late. If תפלה is asking for mercy, there is no deadline.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them (a real doubt in the בית מדרש)
If you will say (granting one side for the sake of argument)
Once its day has passed, its קרבן is cancelled
Asking for mercy
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of the doubt)

steps.confusionAlert: The line starting אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר is not a ruling. It only grants the ערבית-to-שחרית case to show why the מנחה-to-ערבית case might be different.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the practical rule of תשלומין: making up a missed תפלה in the next תפלה.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
One who made a mistake and did not pray מנחה,
what is the law, may he pray two at ערבית?
Even if you will say
that one who made a mistake and did not pray ערבית
prays two at שחרית,
that is because it is one day,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר יוֹם אֶחָד״,
phrases.english: as it is written: "And there was evening and there was morning, one day,"
but here
phrases.notes: "Here" means the missed מנחה case, where the make-up at night is already the next day.

phrases.english: prayer is in place of a קרבן,
and once its day has passed, its קרבן is cancelled.
Or perhaps
since prayer is asking for mercy,
any time he wants, he may keep on praying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from making up שחרית at מנחה to a new case: making up מנחה at ערבית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a missed מנחה be made up at ערבית, even though that is a new day?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules he prays two at ערבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's ruling: one who missed מנחה prays two at ערבית, and the rule of a passed day does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רבי יצחק, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who mistakenly did not pray מנחה prays two at ערבית. The rule that once the day passes the קרבן is cancelled does not apply here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רבי יוחנן: yes, he prays two at ערבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן directly rejects the קרבן comparison for this case. Even though the day has changed, the missed מנחה can still be made up. This fits the side that sees תפלה as asking for mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: Made a mistake, missed it by accident

phrases.english: Come and hear
what רב הונא בר יהודה said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that רבי יצחק said that רבי יוחנן said:
One who made a mistake and did not pray מנחה
prays two at ערבית,
and this does not fall under the rule of
"once its day has passed, its קרבן is cancelled."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A missed מנחה is made up by praying two at ערבית; the passed-day rule of קרבנות does not apply.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a missed תפלה cannot be fixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea of making up a missed תפלה from a ברייתא that explains a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: "What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is missing cannot be counted." "What is crooked cannot be made straight" means someone who skipped night שמע and morning שמע, or the night תפלה or the morning תפלה. "What is missing cannot be counted" means someone whose friends joined together for a מצוה, and he was not counted with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling with a ברייתא that says a skipped תפלה is something that can never be fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists a skipped תפלה as "crooked" that cannot be straightened. That sounds like there is no way to make it up. This seems to contradict the rule that you pray two at the next תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Something crooked, bent
Something missing
Skipped, did not do

phrases.english: They challenged:
"What is crooked cannot be made straight
and what is missing cannot be counted":
"What is crooked cannot be made straight"

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁבִּטֵּל קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁל עַרְבִית
phrases.english: this is one who skipped the night קריאת שמע
and the morning קריאת שמע,
or the night תפלה
or the morning תפלה.
"And what is missing cannot be counted"
this is one whose friends were counted together for a מצוה,
and he was not counted with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a missed תפלה can be made up at the next תפלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls a skipped תפלה something crooked that cannot be fixed, which suggests no make-up is possible.

steps.title: The ברייתא means someone who skipped on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the ברייתא speaks of someone who skipped תפלה on purpose. Only he cannot fix it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What case are we dealing with here? Someone who skipped on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the ברייתא is about someone who skipped תפלה deliberately, not by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources are now true. One who missed by mistake can make it up by praying two next time. One who skipped on purpose has done something crooked that cannot be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows a source to a specific case)
On purpose, deliberately

steps.whatToRemember: One who misses a תפלה by mistake makes it up by praying two at the next תפלה, even from מנחה to ערבית. One who skips on purpose cannot make it up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical rule that תשלומין only helps someone who missed a תפלה by accident.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבי יצחק said that רבי יוחנן said:
What case are we dealing with here?
Where he skipped it on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say any skipped תפלה can never be made up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about skipping on purpose; one who missed by mistake can make it up.

steps.title: רב אשי proves the answer from the exact wording of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי supports רבי יוחנן's answer. The ברייתא says 'בִּטֵּל' (skipped), not 'טָעָה' (made a mistake). So it really is talking only about someone who skipped on purpose. The גמרא concludes: learn from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording is exact too. The ברייתא says 'skipped' and does not say 'made a mistake.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support for רבי יוחנן's answer from the step before. He points out the exact word the ברייתא chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא meant anyone who missed a תפלה, it could have said 'טָעָה'. Instead it said 'בִּטֵּל', which means skipping on purpose. So the rule that a missed תפלה 'cannot be fixed' applies only to someone who skipped on purpose. Someone who missed by mistake can still make it up, as רבי יוחנן ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact. It introduces a proof from the precise words of a source.
Skipped, failed to do. Here it means on purpose.
Made a mistake, missed by error.
Learn from this. The proof is accepted.
It teaches. The source says this.

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who missed a תפלה by mistake can make it up at the next תפלה (רבי יוחנן). Someone who skipped on purpose cannot. The ברייתא's word 'בִּטֵּל' supports this.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not adding a new rule. He is only showing that the ברייתא's own wording backs up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה for תשלומין. A make-up תפלה is allowed for someone who missed by mistake, not for someone who skipped deliberately.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: The wording is also precise,
since it teaches "skipped,"
phrases.notes: This is the word the ברייתא from step 27 used: 'this is one who skipped' קריאת שמע or תפלה.

phrases.english: and it does not teach "made a mistake."
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 28 with a proof from the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's answer that the ברייתא speaks only of someone who skipped תפלה on purpose.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own word choice: 'בִּטֵּל' (skipped) and not 'טָעָה' (erred).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only one who skipped on purpose cannot make up a missed תפלה. One who missed by mistake may make it up.
